drg.description: Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC

notes.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL. Chart, labs and overnight events reviewed. 60-year-old male admitted for urinary tract infection. Admission data:
Day 0: labs bilirubin 0.78, creatinine 0.9-1.06, hemoglobin 14.3-14.4, platelets 226-228, sodium 140, wbc 5.3-5.6; vitals dbp 66-70, heart_rate 82-88, map 84-87, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 16-17, sbp 119-125, spo2 96-98, temp 36.6-36.9
Day 0 orders/meds/results: Urinalysis: positive nitrites, >50 WBC/hpf; Ceftriaxone 1 g IV
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection. Acute kidney injury.

PROGRESS NOTE, hospital day 1. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed. Data:
Day 1: labs creatinine 1.29-1.44, hemoglobin 14.5-14.6, platelets 223-226, sodium 140, wbc 5.7-5.9; vitals dbp 66-71, heart_rate 82-87, map 83-88, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 16-17, sbp 118-123, spo2 96-98, temp 36.7-36.9
Day 1 orders/meds/results: Ceftriaxone 1 g IV; Lactated Ringer's 1 L IV bolus
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection. Acute kidney injury. Continue current management.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY. 60-year-old male, length of stay 4 days. Hospital course: treated per the plan above with daily labs and vital signs; stable for discharge. Medications reconciled and return precautions reviewed. Discharge diagnoses: Urinary tract infection. Acute kidney injury. Follow up with primary care in one week. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed.
